transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm happy to help with any questions you have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling today? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! I'm feeling okay, but I do have a few questions about my recovery. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening, such as watering or weeding, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid heavy digging or lifting for a month. Just remember to be gentle and avoid getting any dirt or water in your eye.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thanks for that. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should have been using preservative-free eye drops four times daily since after your surgery. If you've been using them as directed, you can continue to do so. If you're running out, your GP can provide some more.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thanks for letting me know. I'm also experiencing a lot of sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Some sensitivity to bright light is normal, especially in the first few weeks. Wearing sunglasses can help. If the sensitivity is severe or accompanied by pain, redness, or other symptoms, we may need to assess it further.

transcript.text: Thank you for explaining all of that! I don't have any more questions right now. I appreciate your help.
